# Findings about the site, and the bugs filed for them

The read of the site lists what it found: broken links, pages served under an error, an address of the
site that takes no connection, slow pages, missing security headers, and more.

- `KNOWN-ISSUES.md`: each, with why it matters, the likely fix, every page that shows it, and how the suite treats
  it. Its last section is the team's own, kept by every rebuild.
- `AUDIT.html`: the same, as one page for the site's owner. `crew`, then "Open the site's audit".
- `AUDIT.md`: the same again as Markdown, to send as a link (see "Sending the audit" below).

## Sending the audit

Send the link to AUDIT.md (or the file itself), not a zip of the suite. A person who opens one small Markdown file
reads it safely; a zip is an attachment careful people refuse, and a zip bomb (a small file that unpacks into
something huge) is a real attack.

A link opens for a person with no account only if the repository or gist that holds it is public. So sending an
audit built without --sec means publishing the audit alone, the one file and nothing else of the suite, in a
public place. It is safe to publish because the Markdown writer neutralises the site's own text. Never publish an
audit built with --sec, ever: that audit is private.

## The bugs in bugs/

A finding a test of the suite's own would trip on is filed as a bug, in `bugs/open/`. While it is open, the tests it
breaks are reported as blocked by it, not failed, so a red run still says at a glance whether anything else broke.
A run that no longer sees the finding says so at its end.

- A rebuild from a new read of the site that no longer finds it closes the bug; a line goes into
  `bugs/FIXED.md`.
- You close one by moving its file to `bugs/closed/`; its tests count again. A rebuild that still finds it
  files it again, so it is looked at again.
- Nothing is sent to a tracker on its own: a bug report is yours to write, from the failing test's evidence.

## Pages that are twins

`SITE-GRAPH.md` lists pairs of pages that look like one page copied. Each is tested on what it shows, so a change
made to one and not the other passes both: when one changes, look at the other.
